item.title: First Public Working Draft: Character Model for the World Wide Web: String Matching
item.summary: This document builds upon Character Model for the World Wide Web 1.0: Fundamentals to provide authors of specifications, software developers, and content developers a common reference on string identity matching on the World Wide Web and thereby increase interoperability.

item.title: Proposed Advancement of Web Authentication: An API for accessing Public Key Credentials Level 3 to W3C Recommendation
item.summary: This specification defines an API enabling the creation and use of strong, attested, scoped, public key-based credentials by web applications, for the purpose of strongly authenticating users.

item.title: W3C Invites Implementations of EPUB 3.4, EPUB Reading Systems 3.4 and EPUB Accessibility 1.2
item.summary: EPUB® 3 defines a distribution and interchange format for digital publications and documents. The EPUB format provides a means of representing, packaging, and encoding structured and semantically enhanced web content — including HTML, CSS, SVG, and other resources — for distribution in a single-file container.

item.title: Group Note: WCAG Evaluation Methodology (WCAG-EM) 2.0
item.summary: This document describes a methodology with a step-by-step process to evaluate how well digital products conform to Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) 2.

item.title: Group Note Draft: EPUB Accessibility 1.2 Explainer
item.summary: The EPUB Accessibility 1.2 Explainer provides information on how to understand and evaluate the accessible publications conformance requirements of EPUB Accessibility 1.2 against reflowable EPUB publications.

item.title: Group Note Draft: Verifiable Credentials Overview v1.1
item.summary: The family of W3C Recommendations for Verifiable Credentials, described in this overview document, provides a mechanism to express these sorts of credentials on the Web in a way that is cryptographically secure, privacy respecting, and machine-verifiable.

item.title: W3C Invites Implementations of WebTransport
item.summary: This document defines a set of ECMAScript APIs in WebIDL to allow data to be sent and received between a browser and server.

item.title: Group Note: Further Aligning W3C's Program of Technical Work with Human Rights
item.summary: In this document, the Advisory Board lists examples of how human rights and technical standards setting map to each other, points to existing W3C work in this area, and provides concrete proposals to further the alignment between the W3C’s technical work and human rights.

item.title: W3C invites implementations of Decentralized Identifier Resolution (DID Resolution) v1
item.summary: This document describes the process of obtaining a DID document and accompanying metadata for a specific DID.

item.title: Updated W3C Recommendation: ARIA in HTML
item.summary: This specification defines the authoring rules (author conformance requirements) for the use of Accessible Rich Internet Applications (WAI-ARIA) 1.2 and Digital Publishing WAI-ARIA Module 1.1 attributes on [HTML] elements.

item.title: Group Note Draft: Web Sustainability Guidelines (WSG) Impact Ratings
item.summary: This document describes the impact ratings provided alongside Web Sustainability Guidelines (WSG).

item.title: First Public Working Draft: The Profiles Vocabulary
item.summary: The Profiles Vocabulary is an RDF vocabulary created to allow the machine-readable description of profiles of specifications for information resources.

item.title: Patent Advisory Group recommends continuing work on Open Screen Application Protocol
item.summary: W3C launches a Patent Advisory Group (PAG) to resolve issues in the event a patent has been disclosed that may be essential, but is not available under the W3C Royalty-Free licensing terms.

item.title: Web Authentication: An API for accessing Public Key Credentials Level 3 is now a W3C Recommendation
item.summary: This specification defines an API enabling the creation and use of strong, attested, scoped, public key-based credentials by web applications, for the purpose of strongly authenticating users.

item.title: W3C opens 2026 community survey
item.summary: W3C opens an 8-minute survey until 30 September and seeks community-wide input to get to know our community better, investigate needs, and understand how we can improve.

item.title: First Public Working Draft: Web Authentication: An API for accessing Public Key Credentials Level 4
item.summary: This specification defines an API enabling the creation and use of strong, attested, scoped, public key-based credentials by web applications, for the purpose of strongly authenticating users.

item.title: First Public Working Draft: SHACL 1.2 Inference Rules
item.summary: This document defines the Inference Rules support of the SHACL Shapes Constraint Language (SHACL).

item.title: Authorized Translations of WCAG 2.2 and 2.1 in French updated
item.summary: W3C has published the updated Authorized French Translations of Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) 2.2 and 2.1.

item.title: Group Note Draft: Verifiable Credentials Data Model Threat Model v2.1
item.summary: This document describes a threat model for the Verifiable Credentials Data Model specification.

item.title: First Public Working Draft: Bitstring Status List v1.1
item.summary: This specification describes a privacy-preserving, space-efficient, and high-performance mechanism for publishing status information such as suspension or revocation of Verifiable Credentials through use of bitstrings.

item.title: W3C Workshop Report: The Future of ODRL
item.summary: W3C is pleased to announce the report from the W3C Workshop on the Future of ODRL, held in July 2026 in London, UK, and online.

item.title: Consortium Members elect Board of Directors
item.summary: World Wide Web Consortium Members have elected seven individuals to the World Wide Web Consortium, Inc. Board of Directors

item.title: Updated Candidate Recommendation: Scalable Vector Graphics (SVG) 2
item.summary: The SVG Working Group published Scalable Vector Graphics (SVG) 2 as a Candidate Recommendation Snapshot and invites implementations.

item.title: W3C issues press release about developing Verifiable Credential Barcodes
item.summary: In a press release we present the concept of real-time revocation that is being developed in the W3C Verifiable Credentials Barcodes specification to protect physical documents.

item.title: First Draft Notes: Verifiable Credential Threat Models
item.summary: The Verifiable Credentials Working Group has published a series of W3C Working Group Note Drafts for threat models.
